correctness.rationale: The cofactor formula gives S(u)=pi sqrt(abc)/sqrt(u^T Q u), P(u)=pi sqrt(abc)sqrt(u^T Q^-1u), so Z=(u^T Q u)(u^T Q^-1u)=1+A w1w2+B w1w3+C w2w3, w_i=u_i^2. Kantorovich AM-GM gives K=(a+c)^2/(4ac), attained at exactly four directions with u2=0 and |u1|=|u3|=1/sqrt2. Local spherical coordinates have Haar density dtheta dy/(4pi), deficit B s^2+D y^2+O((|s|+|y|)^3), D=(B-A-C)/2=(b-a)(a+c)(c-b)/(2abc)>0; summing four ellipse-cap areas gives gamma=1/sqrt(BD). The endpoint k=c/a recovered from K; gamma fixes t+k/t, giving precisely t and k/t, the unavoidable polar alternatives. Independently verified all algebra by symbolic factorization and the exact gamma values at (1,2,3),(2,3,7),(1,4,25), including example K=4/3,gamma=3/2.

originality.rationale: Classical Kantorovich gives the max K but not two-dimensional Hessian coefficient or inversion from it. Kim-Yaskin-Zvavitch examine marginal area distributions for sections or projections, not the paired same-direction quotient. Resultary inverse-square section moments determine ellipsoid axes via a different measurement, and Fish et al study parallel section functions. No read source subsumes the paired upper-tail slope and polar-ambiguous inversion. An older general product-quadratic-form density might, so best-knowledge risk remains.
